answer: Slashable stake escrows mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital before transacting. Across a nebula of peers, bonded capital acts as structural timber for network trust, forcing adversaries to incur the verifiable opportunity cost of locked liquidity per identity. When raven audit sentinels detect coordinated fraud, offending bonds are slashed. However, well-funded cartels can still absorb deposit costs, and mandatory staking unfairly penalizes resource-poor agents.
